title: JSON, List, Record, Textable
documentation:
## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

JavaScript Object Notation. Text-based, human-readable, ubiquitous. The default
serialization for structured cap inputs and outputs.

## List marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is an ordered sequence at its
root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.
Independent of `record-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate
elements in order.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.
